expected_shape.what: TEN CKAN DataStore layers from ONE package, decided TOGETHER (R2-12, 0y skip_scope all_primaries): one package_show reads every resource's version; the run skips only when all ten equal records_meta.zoning_layer_versions and the 730-day window has not elapsed. The NORMAL run is that skip (the City republishes about once a year): four pre rows (licence, force override, no_op_refresh true, dataset_version_age_days), null counters, and the prior run's five §9 keys re-emitted. A changed or forced run pages every layer through datastore_search and writes each in its own transaction: base 11,719 rows, overlays 4 to 8,913, about 87 audit rows.

measured.query: SELECT COUNT(*) per zoning table = each resource's datastore_search total (re-grounding .cursor/zoning-plan-regrounding-2026-10-02.md §B :13)

read_this_way.what: Q1 — ONE shapeRecord serves all ten primaries and tells a record's layer by its own CKAN fields: the runner seam hands it {geojson, config, run_at, tag} and no external id. Each layer is recognised by a field no other layer's column set carries (GEN_ZONE / ZN_ZONE … for the base, HT_LABEL for height, PRCNT_CVER for lot coverage, CH600_LINE_TYPE for priority retail, ZN_PARKZONE for parking, …). building_setback_overlay and queenstw_eat_overlay have IDENTICAL field sets and column maps, so they share one signature and shape identically; their per-layer counts still come from each primary's own acquired block. A record that matches no signature is skipped as unroutable_record (shaped_skipped_by_reason), never guessed.

The column vocabulary (LAYER_COLUMNS in the compute) is DOMAIN DATA: CKAN field → target column, kind, and the migration-164 CHECK mirror (min / max / maxLen). D9: an out-of-range numeric cell — Toronto's pervasive -1 'not regulated' sentinel — is nulled and the row kept (counted as <layer>_out_of_range_nulled_count, INFO). R2-16: HT_LABEL parses only a plain number of metres; a range like '10-12' leaves height_max_m NULL and counts as unparseable. TEXT columns are truncated to maxLen (zn_zone 20, base zn_string 50).

constants.what: The external ids are the frozen legacy layer keys (base, height_overlay, …) because zoning_layers_loaded / zoning_layer_versions / zoning_partial_load are keyed by them (Spec 58 §9). The audit metrics keep the legacy names: the base layer's rows are zoning_areas_*, an overlay's are <layer key>_*. MS_PER_DAY comes from scripts/lib/units.js; every bound is one of the fifteen load_zoning_* logic variables, defaults byte-equal to the legacy literals except load_zoning_http_timeout_ms (60000, a whole-request deadline replacing the 30 s socket-idle timeout, LZ-D15).

known_normal.what: coverage_max_pct_null_count = every base row is NORMAL (Spec 58 §11 D10: Toronto leaves COVERAGE blank; coverage lives in zoning_lot_coverage_overlay). fsi_max is non-null on about 2,835 base rows. zoning_areas_out_of_range_nulled_count in the tens of thousands is normal (the -1 sentinel is pervasive). zoning_height_overlay_unparseable_label_count > 0 WARN is a known, standing source condition (range labels).

measured.query: re-grounding §B :59 (fsi non-null / coverage NULL) + run 1085 audit rows (plan §7 bounds table)

suspicious_if.what: zoning_areas_attr_drift or zoning_overlay_attr_drift > 0 means CKAN renamed or dropped a mapped field: the base FAILs before any write (D3), an overlay's write is skipped and it reads false in zoning_layers_loaded. primary_failed:<layer> WARN means that overlay's datastore_search threw (a CKAN 504 is common, re-grounding A12) and zoning_partial_load lists it; enrich_parcels then treats that overlay as stale. A FORCED run that writes rows on every layer although the source is unchanged is the 121-row GEOS vertex-order drift (re-grounding A2), not a data change.

blind_spots.what: LZ-D3: drift is read from each layer's FIRST raw record only. LZ-D7: the loaded_pct / null-count / exceptions / duration baselines read the latest successful run, which after a skip carries none of them, so the first load after a skip has no baseline. LZ-D2: source_dataset_version is not a guard column, so an unchanged row keeps the stamp of the load that last changed it. LZ-D12: a drift-skipped overlay still records its new version, so the next run may skip it (④d).

decisions.what: Failure posture is legacy parity (D3): the base primary declares no on_failure (abort_step) — its fetch, drift, empty-source or write failure fails the step and no overlay is acquired; every overlay declares warn_row_continue — its failure is a WARN row, the run continues, and base_layer_committed_after_overlays_failed reads true. A package_show failure fails the step by name before any datastore_search (LZ-D6, ④a retired). Q3: execution.txn_scope is batch — one transaction per target, ten per load (the POST witness trace is the final confirmation).

fences.value: externals[base] has no on_failure (abort_step); externals[overlays].on_failure = warn_row_continue; zoning_areas_attr_drift + zoning_areas_loaded_count are FAIL pre_write gates
